# requireNonInteger

<link-summary>Returns the value after checking that it is not an integer.</link-summary>

<web-summary>requireNonInteger() — Returns the value after checking that it is not an integer. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>lang/number</code> · Since: 1.11.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function requireNonInteger<T>(
  value: T | number,
  message: string = "Expected a value that is not an integer."
): T;
```

A number with no fractional part. Nothing is coerced, so the string `"42"` is not an integer, and `NaN` is not either.

`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

## Parameters

| Parameter                                                             | Type          | Description                                                   |
| :-------------------------------------------------------------------- | :------------ | :------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `value`                                                               | `T \| number` | The value to validate.                                        |
| `message` _(optional)_ `= "Expected a value that is not an integer."` | `string`      | The message of the exception. A default is used when omitted. |

## Returns

`T` — the same value, with an integer excluded from its type.

## Throws

| Exception                  | Condition                |
| :------------------------- | :----------------------- |
| `IllegalArgumentException` | the value is an integer. |

## Examples

### What passes and what does not

```javascript
requireNonInteger(1.5); // => 1.5
requireNonInteger(NaN); // => NaN
requireNonInteger(42); // throws IllegalArgumentException
requireNonInteger(-7); // throws IllegalArgumentException
```
